text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Cabinet agrees to provide more funds and manpower to the Anti-Corruption Agency to fight graft more effectively.
-- The Road Transport Department will be given the power to suspend the licences of drivers involved in fatal accidents.
-- Malaysia Airlines will hold talks with Kuwait Airlines seeking ways to resume air services between the two countries.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says the stock market will rebound after plummeting to a six-month last week.
-- State oil firm Petronas and the Kuwait Petroleum Company will co-operate to initiate possible upstream and downstream ventures locally and in developing countries.
